lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Gerald, this is Kendra. Is this an okay time to talk?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, sorry, I'm in the car but I can talk.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Here's what I had in mind for today, but tell me if you'd rather focus on something else.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How's your body feeling this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Kind of down this week.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That sounds like a hard week.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What happened with the overnight fast?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good! I didn't miss a day.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'd like to be able to keep up with my grandkids. I feel guilty when I skip it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good for you for planning ahead.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've always eaten late, that's how we do it at home.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've tried before and it didn't stick.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My sugar was better the weeks I ate earlier.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Black coffee, tea or water are fine during the fast. They don't break it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe after the summer.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So it's not that you don't care. It's that the parties keeps getting in the way.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So, I'm too tired for this right now.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you mind if I tell you what some people do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Finishing dinner a little earlier, like by 7, makes the 13 hours a lot easier.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Getting back to work is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This is about more than the overnight fast. It's about getting your life back.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I like what I eat. I'm not going to change at my age.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're not sure it's worth it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Walking hurts my knees, so why bother.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is coffee with milk the first thing you have?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really want to feel like myself again. I wrote it on the calendar.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, yes. We had a birthday party, there was so much food.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Black coffee, tea or water are fine during the fast. They don't break it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I told my family I'm done eating at 8. I don't want to end up like my dad.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've already started.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Everybody gets home late, so dinner is late.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the overnight fast fit in your day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know I can do it, I did it before.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Next week I want you to finish eating by 7:30 on 4 nights.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Like a 6.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why a 6 and not a 3?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If I plan it the night before, I can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll ask my son to come with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So, to sum up: the parties made this week harder, you still got 3 days in, and your plan is to finish eating by 7:30 on 4 nights. Sound right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That's it exactly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Wednesday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Gerald, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thanks, bye bye.

flags.reason: Coach sets the 7:30 four-night goal directly after participant said 'I don't know'; no collaboration or permission before setting it.
Participant's 'getting back to work' motivation was not explored; coach jumped to 'getting your life back' framing, which led to sustain talk.
Participant said 'kind of down this week'; coach moved on without asking about mood or energy, a possible low-mood cue to check.

score.summary: Kendra used good reflections and affirmations, and the participant moved from sustain talk to a concrete plan with a barrier identified by the end. However, she set the four-night goal directly, and she passed over the 'kind of down' cue and his 'getting back to work' motivation without exploring them.
strengths: Line 12: 'Good for you for planning ahead' affirms effort appropriately.
Line 20 and 41: asked permission ('Can I share an idea?') before offering coffee/tea guidance.
Line 52-56: scaling question followed by 'Why a 6 and not a 3?' drew out confidence and self-efficacy talk.
Line 58: clear summary that closed the conversation with the participant's agreement.
coaching_tips: Line 50: Offer the next-week goal as a question ('What feels doable for next week?') rather than stating 'I want you to.'
Line 28: Reflect the participant's own motivation ('getting back to work') before reframing to 'life back'.
Line 6: Follow up on 'kind of down' with an open question about mood and energy before moving on.
Line 37 and 44: 'I see' and 'Okay' are filler; a short reflection would deepen the conversation.
